title: Kingdom of Laos

endonym.native: ພຣະຣາຊອານາຈັກລາວ

capsule: The Kingdom of Laos was a constitutional monarchy established in 1947 when France granted internal autonomy within the French Union, with King Sisavang Vong as head of state; full independence was recognised in 1953. The country was drawn into the Second Indochina War, with the Pathet Lao communist movement — backed by North Vietnam — contesting control of the country throughout the 1960s and early 1970s alongside intense U.S. bombing. Following the fall of Saigon in April 1975, the Pathet Lao completed their takeover and King Savang Vatthana abdicated in December 1975, ending the monarchy and establishing the Lao People's Democratic Republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's territorial extent is well documented by French colonial maps and post-independence surveys, but effective government control varied widely by region due to the civil war.
